what: a 3 mm chamfer on the rim of a hole tangent to the bottom face runs off that face: refused, because the back face narrows to a point where the rim touches the bottom edge tangentially (never material added below the part)
method: cube 20 with a diameter 10 hole along -Y from the back face, its axis at z=5 so the hole wall touches the bottom face z=0 along one line. The hole rim on the back face has no face material between it and the bottom edge there, so a 3 mm setback cannot lie on the face: no chamfer of that size exists. The right answer is a clean refusal (a chamfer of a convex edge only ever removes material; building it grew the part by 1067 mm3 below the bottom face). It is refused at the vertex where the rim touches the bottom edge tangentially: the back face narrows to a point there, so no chamfer of any size fits, and the refusal says so (#16404).
